think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 67-year-old man on cumulative immunosuppressive therapy for refractory Crohn's disease (JAK inhibitor upadacitinib plus systemic corticosteroids) developed subcarinal lymphadenopathy and destructive paravertebral osteolytic lesions mimicking metastatic malignancy, despite having completed prophylactic isoniazid for latent tuberculosis two years prior.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Presentation with progressive back pain, fatigue, focal midthoracic tenderness, elevated ESR/CRP, and contrast chest CT showing subcarinal lymphadenopathy and an upper mediastinal mass with vertebral destruction, prior to bronchoscopy with EBUS-TDB core biopsy and molecular testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Metastatic spinal malignancy was ruled out by negative serum tumor markers, benign fibrous histology on core biopsy, and negative cytology; invasive fungal infection was ruled out by negative galactomannan, fungal cultures, and negative silver staining; reactivation occurred due to potent JAK-inhibitor immunosuppression breaking latent containment.
case_prompt: A 67-year-old man with refractory Crohn's disease maintained on chronic cumulative immunosuppressive therapy—including the oral Janus kinase inhibitor upadacitinib (30 mg daily) and maintenance low-dose systemic corticosteroids, following prior anti-TNF and IL-12/23 biologic agents—presented with a 6-month history of insidious clinical deterioration, characterized by progressive thoracic back pain and generalized fatigue. He reported no fever, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, cough, or hemoptysis. Two years earlier, he had completed a full prophylactic course of isoniazid monotherapy after routine pre-biologic screening identified latent infection. On physical examination, he was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Examination of the spine revealed a noticeable thoracic deformity with focal bony tenderness on palpation over the midthoracic vertebrae, without neurological deficits. Initial laboratory studies revealed a normal white blood cell count of 7.3 × 10⁹/L without neutrophilia or left shift, mild normocytic anemia with hemoglobin of 117 g/L (MCV 86.6 fL), normal platelet count, and normal serum electrolytes, renal function, and hepatic enzymes. Inflammatory markers were elevated, with a C-reactive protein of 15.57 mg/L and erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 35 mm/h. Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography revealed progression of subcarinal lymphadenopathy and an upper mediastinal paravertebral soft-tissue mass with adjacent osteolytic vertebral destruction.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Metastatic spinal malignancy or primary mediastinal neoplasm
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Aggressive osteolytic vertebral destruction, paravertebral mass, and subcarinal lymphadenopathy strongly simulated advanced metastatic disease; however, an extensive panel of serum tumor markers was entirely normal, and mediastinal lymph node core biopsy cytology and immunohistochemistry showed no neoplastic cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: These imaging findings raised a strong suspicion of malignancy, particularly metastatic disease. Given the aggressive radiological features, metastatic malignancy was the primary diagnostic consideration... an extensive tumor marker panel... yielded entirely normal results, arguing against an underlying metastatic malignancy... Liquid-based cytology specimens from lymph node stations 2R, 4R, and 7 were negative for malignancy.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe cumulative immunosuppression from a JAK inhibitor and corticosteroids; however, fungal blood/sputum cultures, serum galactomannan assay, and special fungal staining (PAS and Grocott-methenamine silver) on lymph node tissue were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A dedicated fungal workup was subsequently performed, including sputum fungal smear, galactomannan assay, and fungal culture, all of which were negative... both periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and PAS-methenamine silver staining were negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Autoimmune serologies including antinuclear antibodies and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative, and the lesion demonstrated destructive bone invasion and progressive cold abscess formation rather than enteropathic arthritis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Serum anti-tuberculosis antibody testing was positive, whereas autoimmune screening (antinuclear antibodies and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies) was negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In this patient under cumulative immunosuppression with upadacitinib and corticosteroids, EBUS-guided transbronchial mediastinal lymph node core biopsy (EBUS-TDB) demonstrated Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA on Xpert MTB/RIF assay, establishing mediastinal tuberculous lymphadenitis with paravertebral cold abscess and Pott's disease.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Crucially, the Xpert MTB/RIF assay on lymph node tissue detected Mycobacterium TB complex DNA at a trace level. Integrating the clinical context, radiological findings, and molecular evidence, a diagnosis of MTL complicated by a paravertebral cold abscess and secondary vertebral osteomyelitis (Pott's disease) was established.

editor_comments: Tumor-like tuberculous lymphadenitis with Pott's disease developing under cumulative immunosuppression with upadacitinib despite previous completion of isoniazid prophylaxis.
